about: Golden vectors for splits, bonus shares, rights and transfers (PA2: F7, C1-C9, TF1-TF8). The numbers are derived by hand in each case's 'why'; make_pa2.py writes this file, imports nothing from sudarshan, and the tests hold the engine and a naive second implementation to it. Synthetic data only. A case's 'decimals' says how many decimals a quantity of the asset may have (shares 0) and 'over_year_on' asks each position for the units held for more than a year on that day.

cases.title: A transfer between accounts keeps the lot's cost and day
cases.why: Account 1 buys 10 on 5 Jan 2024 for 1,000.00 (100000 paise). On 1 Jun 2025 all 10 move to account 2: the one lot goes whole, so it takes its whole cost 100000 and keeps its day (5 Jan 2024). Account 2 sells 10 on 1 Jul 2025 for 1,500.00 (150000): that lot costs 100000, gain 150000 - 100000 = 50000 (500.00). A transfer is no sale: it makes no gain.

words.2: From 5 Jan 2024: 10 at ₹100.00 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: A lot moved to another account is still held for more than a year from its first day
cases.why: The same entries up to the transfer (as of 1 Jun 2025). The lot is account 2's now, dated 5 Jan 2024. Its first anniversary was 5 Jan 2025, and 1 Jun 2025 is after it: all 10 units have been held for more than a year. Account 1 holds nothing.

cases.title: On the first anniversary itself a lot is not yet held for more than a year
cases.why: The same position looked at on 5 Jan 2025, the first anniversary of the 5 Jan 2024 purchase: it has been held for exactly a year, not more than a year, so 0 units count.

cases.title: A split keeps the cost and the day: each share becomes 5
cases.why: Buy 10 on 1 May 2023 for 10,000.00 (1,000,000 paise). On 10 Mar 2025 each share becomes 5: 10 x 5 = 50 units. The lot keeps its cost 1,000,000 and its day, so a unit now costs 1,000,000 / 50 = 20,000 paise (200.00).

words.2: Each share becomes 5 · 10 become 50 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: A sale after a split takes its cost at the new unit cost
cases.why: After C1 the lot is 50 units costing 1,000,000. A sale of 20 on 1 Apr 2025 for 4,500.00 (450000) takes 1,000,000 x 20/50 = 400,000 of the cost (200.00 a unit); gain 450000 - 400000 = 50000 (500.00). Left: 30 units costing 600,000, still dated 1 May 2023.

cases.title: A consolidation that would leave part of a share is refused
cases.why: Buy 15 shares. A split of 1 new for every 10 old would leave 15 x 1/10 = 1.5 shares, and shares are whole numbers (0 decimals). The split is entry 2 and is the one named, with the account it fails in.

refused.message: This split would leave 1.5 shares in Zerodha. Record the sale of the fraction first, then the split.

cases.title: The same consolidation is fine for fund units, which have four decimals
cases.why: 15 units, 1 new for every 10 old: 1.5 units, which four decimals can hold (1.5000). The lot keeps its cost 150000 and its day.

words.2: 1 new for every 10 old · 15 become 1.5 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: Two lots of 5 consolidated 1 for 10 are two lots of half a share that make one share
cases.why: Buy 5 for 500.00 (50000) on 6 Jan 2025 and 5 for 600.00 (60000) on 10 Feb. A split of 1 new for every 10 old: 10 x 1/10 = 1 share, whole. The lots become 0.5 and 0.5 (500000 each) with their cost and day. Selling the 1 share for 200.00 (20000) takes both: cost 50000 + 60000 = 110000, loss 20000 - 110000 = -90000 (900.00).

words.3: 1 new for every 10 old · 10 become 1 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: Lots that do not divide are rounded on the running total, so the share count is exact
cases.why: Buy 7 (70000) and 8 (96000). A split of 1 new for every 3 old: 15 x 1/3 = 5 shares, whole. The first lot alone would be 7/3 = 2.333333 (2,333,333 in millionths, rounded); the two together are exactly 5,000,000, so the second lot is 5,000,000 - 2,333,333 = 2,666,667. Lots 2,333,333 + 2,666,667 = 5,000,000, cost kept: 70000 and 96000.

words.3: 1 new for every 3 old · 15 become 5 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: Three lots that each round down would make less than a whole share, so the running total is used
cases.why: Three lots of 1 share cost 100.00, 110.00 and 120.00 (10000, 11000, 12000). One new share for every 3 old: 3 x 1/3 = 1 share, whole. Each lot alone would be 1/3 = 0.333333 (333,333 millionths), and three of those make 999,999, not 1,000,000. Rounding the running total instead: 1,000,000 x 1/3 = 333,333 after the first lot, 2,000,000 x 1/3 = 666,667 after the second (so the second takes 333,334), 3,000,000 x 1/3 = 1,000,000 after the third (333,333). The lots add up to exactly 1 share and keep their cost and day. Selling that share for 400.00 (40000) takes all three: cost 10000 + 11000 + 12000 = 33000, gain 40000 - 33000 = 7000.

words.4: 1 new for every 3 old · 3 become 1 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: A split without an account applies to every account that holds the asset
cases.why: Account 1 holds 10 (100000), account 2 holds 4 (44000). Each share becomes 2 on 10 Mar 2025, for every account: 20 and 8 units, each lot keeping its cost and day. One move for each account, the lower account number first.

words.3: Each share becomes 2 · 10 become 20 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: A split for one account leaves the others alone
cases.why: The same holdings, but the split names account 1: it goes to 20 units, account 2 keeps its 4 units and 44000.

cases.title: A split for every account is refused for the account that cannot take it
cases.why: Account 1 holds 10 shares, account 2 holds 3. One new share for every 5 old: account 1 would hold 10 x 1/5 = 2, which is whole, but account 2 would hold 3 x 1/5 = 0.6. The split is refused for the account it fails in (Account B), and no account changes.

refused.message: This split would leave 0.6 shares in Account B. Record the sale of the fraction first, then the split.

cases.title: A split in an account that holds none of the asset is refused
cases.why: Only account 2 bought. A split named for account 1 on 12 Mar 2025 has nothing to split.

refused.message: Zerodha holds no RELIANCE on 12 Mar 2025, so a split cannot be saved. Check the date, or add the missing purchase first.

cases.title: A split for every account is refused when no account holds the asset
cases.why: Nothing was bought, so a split for every account has nothing to split.

refused.message: No account holds RELIANCE on 12 Mar 2025, so a split cannot be saved. Check the date, or add the missing purchase first.

cases.title: A bonus in an account that holds none of the asset is refused
cases.why: Only account 2 bought; account 1 cannot receive bonus shares on shares it never held.

refused.message: Zerodha holds no RELIANCE on 12 Mar 2025, so a bonus cannot be saved. Check the date, or add the missing purchase first.

cases.title: A bonus dated after the account sold out is refused
cases.why: Buy 10 on 10 Jan, sell all 10 on 1 Mar: on 12 Mar the account holds none, so a bonus dated 12 Mar is refused (the sentence asks the owner to check the date).

refused.message: Zerodha holds no RELIANCE on 12 Mar 2025, so a bonus cannot be saved. Check the date, or add the missing purchase first.

cases.title: Bonus shares are a new lot at nil cost, dated the allotment
cases.why: Buy 10 on 1 May 2023 for 1,000.00 (100000). Bonus of 10 allotted on 15 Sep 2025: a new lot of 10 costing 0, dated 15 Sep 2025. 20 units, cost still 100000.

cases.title: A sale after a bonus takes the older lot first, then the nil-cost bonus lot
cases.why: After C3, sell 15 on 20 Oct 2025 for 1,050.00 (105000). FIFO: the whole 1 May 2023 lot (10 units, 100000), then 5 of the bonus lot, whose cost is 0 x 5/10 = 0. Cost 100000, gain 105000 - 100000 = 5000 (50.00). Left: 5 bonus units at no cost.

cases.title: A rights issue is a purchase: a new lot at the price paid
cases.why: Buy 10 (100000). Rights of 2 at 80.00 on 1 Jun 2025 cost 160.00 (16000): a new lot of 2 costing 16000, dated 1 Jun 2025. 12 units, cost 116000.

cases.title: On the day of a split the split is applied first, whatever was typed first
cases.why: Buy 10 on 6 Jan (100000). On 10 Mar a purchase of 4 for 600.00 (60000) is typed before the split (each share becomes 2) that takes effect that morning. The split goes first: 10 -> 20, then the 4 are bought: 24 units, cost 160000. Applying the split after the purchase would double the 4 as well (28).

cases.title: A lot moved in parts gives the new account its share of the cost, rounded as a sale is
cases.why: Account 1 buys 3 for 100.00 (10000) on 6 Jan 2025. Moving 1 unit takes 10000 x 1/3 = 3333.33 -> 3333 (account 1 keeps 2 units and 6667). Moving 1 more takes 6667 x 1/2 = 3333.5 -> 3334 (half away from zero; account 1 keeps 1 unit and 3333). Account 2 now holds two lots dated 6 Jan, 3333 and 3334, in the order they arrived. Selling both for 90.00 (9000) uses 3333 + 3334 = 6667; gain 9000 - 6667 = 2333. Cost is never lost: 3333 + 6667 = 10000.

words.2: From 6 Jan 2025: 1 at ₹33.33 · cost and dates kept

cases.title: Shares brought in from outside open a lot at the cost entered, dated their first purchase
cases.why: Account 1 is given 10 shares from outside on 1 Apr 2026: cost 1,000.00 (100000), first bought 15 Aug 2023, worth 1,500.00 that day (150000, which is what counts as money in; the lot's cost stays 100000). Selling 4 on 15 Sep 2026 for 700.00 (70000) takes 100000 x 4/10 = 40000; gain 70000 - 40000 = 30000 (300.00). Left: 6 units, 60000, still dated 15 Aug 2023.

cases.title: Without a first-purchase date or a value, the lot is dated the transfer and worth its cost
cases.why: 10 shares come in from outside on 1 Apr 2026 at a cost of 1,000.00 (100000), with no original date and no value: the lot is dated 1 Apr 2026 and the money counted in is its cost, 100000.

cases.title: An opening lot with an earlier first-purchase date is sold before a lot bought after it
cases.why: Account 1 buys 5 on 1 Mar 2025 (50000). On 1 Apr 2025 5 more come in from outside at a cost of 400.00 (40000), first bought 15 Jan 2024. FIFO goes by the day a lot was bought, so a sale of 5 on 15 Apr 2025 for 700.00 (70000) takes the 15 Jan 2024 lot: cost 40000, gain 30000. The 1 Mar lot is left whole.

cases.title: Shares taken out to outside leave at their cost, with no gain or loss
cases.why: Buy 10 (100000) on 10 Jan and 10 (120000) on 10 Feb 2025. On 10 Mar 15 shares leave the tab: the whole 10 Jan lot (100000) and 5 of the 10 Feb lot (120000 x 5/10 = 60000). Cost 160000 leaves with them; there is no gain or loss, and with no value entered the money counted out is that cost. Left: 5 units, 60000.

words.3: From 10 Jan 2025: 10 at ₹100.00; from 10 Feb 2025: 5 at ₹120.00 · left at cost, no gain or loss

cases.title: A value entered for shares taken out changes the money counted out, not the gain
cases.why: The same transfer out, entered with a value of 1,950.00 (195000): that is the money counted out, but the lots still leave at their cost 160000 and the gain stays 0.

cases.title: Moving more than the account holds is refused, in words
cases.why: Account 1 holds 10 on 12 Mar 2025; a transfer of 12 is 2 short. The transfer is entry 2.

refused.message: Zerodha holds 10 RELIANCE on 12 Mar 2025, so a transfer of 12 cannot be saved. Add the missing purchase first.

cases.title: On one day a purchase, then the move, then the sale of the moved shares
cases.why: On 10 Mar 2025, typed in the opposite order: sell 5 in account 2 (600.00, 60000), move 10 from account 1 to 2, buy 10 in account 1 (1,000.00, 100000). The day applies the purchase, then the move, then the sale, so it stands: account 2 holds the 10 at 100000 and the sale takes 100000 x 5/10 = 50000; gain 60000 - 50000 = 10000. Account 2 is left with 5 units and 50000.

cases.title: A moved lot takes its place in the new account by the day it was bought
cases.why: Account 1 buys 2 on 6 Jan 2025 (20000); account 2 buys 2 on 1 Mar 2025 (30000). On 1 Apr the 6 Jan lot moves to account 2, where it goes ahead of the 1 Mar lot because it is older. A sale of 1 on 15 Apr for 180.00 (18000) takes the 6 Jan lot: 20000 x 1/2 = 10000, gain 8000. Left in account 2: 1 unit at 10000 (6 Jan) and 2 at 30000 (1 Mar).
